problem_statement: The Fathom Dispatch is a real Jekyll build served as a multi-page static editorial blog (a home page at /index.html, a Field Dispatches index at /posts/, a masthead page at /about.html, and the individual dated dispatch pages, all sharing the top navigation and footer). A recent design change added a native topic filter to the Field Dispatches index (styled by assets/dispatch-filter.css and wired by assets/dispatch-filter.js) that lets a reader narrow the post list to Exploration, Science, or Reflection and shows a live count readout ('Showing N of 6 · Topic'). The filter's chip row was laid out as a fixed-width, non-wrapping strip, so it cannot shrink and the Field Dispatches page overflows horizontally on a 390px phone while the desktop and tablet layouts still contain it. The same change was meant to add a shared 'Dispatch desk' rail to the site footer so it appears on every editorial page (home, Field Dispatches, and the masthead), but in the shipped state the rail only renders on the home page and is missing from the other pages, and the topic filter's count readout does not update when a topic chip is clicked. Restyle the topic filter so the Field Dispatches page fits a phone with no horizontal overflow and stays legible and on-brand, keep the shared dispatch rail present on every page, and keep the topic filter's readout in sync with the selected chip — preserving the Clean Blog editorial visual language, the six dispatches, the masthead copy, and the bundled local photographs.
required_content: Restyle the topic-filter chip row so the mobile (390px) Field Dispatches page has no horizontal overflow (document scrollWidth within 24px of the viewport), while keeping the desktop and tablet layouts intact.

Keep the four topic chips visible and legible (All, Exploration, Science, Reflection) with readable contrast, and keep the six dispatch cards laid out as a clean readable list, not an overlapping pile.
Keep the shared 'Dispatch desk' rail (labelled The Dispatch Desk) present in the footer of every page: the home page AND the Field Dispatches index AND the masthead page.

Keep the topic filter functional so its count readout updates to the selected topic (for example 'Showing 2 of 6 · Science') after a topic chip is clicked, not frozen on 'Showing 6 of 6 · All dispatches'.
Preserve the original editorial content signals The Fathom Dispatch, Filter dispatches by topic, the six dispatch titles, the Posted by bylines, and the masthead copy.
Keep the bundled local dispatch photographs under img/posts/ as browser-visible img elements on the dispatch pages.
Do not remove content, add a framework/package-manager/backend/remote API/remote image/new dependency, or introduce console or network errors.
The restyle must be a scoped responsive-layout + wiring fix, not a content rewrite, and must not change the page content or DOM structure across viewports.
design_constraints: Fix the topic-filter chip row's flex layout so the chips wrap/flex fluidly on narrow viewports instead of pinning a fixed row width; use stable responsive constraints and normal media queries.

Keep the Clean Blog editorial visual language: serif headings, generous whitespace, teal accent, a clean single-column reading rhythm for the dispatch cards, and legible text contrast. Do not restyle the filter into a dark, low-contrast slab where chips shingle over each other and cards collide into an illegible pile.
Render the shared dispatch rail on every page's footer, not only the home page, so the cross-page editorial identity stays consistent.
Wire the topic filter so the count readout reflects the live result each time a chip is clicked; do not leave a stale readout that never updates.
Do not use viewport-width font scaling, hidden-only benchmark text, placeholder images, remote stock media, or overflow-x:hidden hacks that leave the underlying fixed-width row overflowing.
state_constraints: desktop_initial, tablet_initial, and mobile_initial verify the editorial home page loads across breakpoints with no horizontal overflow after the restyle.

mobile_posts_filter verifies the restyled topic-filter chip row fits a 390px phone with no horizontal overflow; the original-with-defect leg overflows about 385px and the broken restyle overflows about 419px.

desktop_posts_filter verifies the topic filter keeps the Clean Blog editorial visual language (legible chips, teal active state, readable spaced dispatch cards) and reads as coherent editorial design, not a dark collapsed slab.
desktop_posts_science verifies the topic filter's count readout updates after the Science chip is clicked (interaction continuity).
desktop_home_rail, desktop_about_rail, and desktop_posts_filter verify the shared dispatch rail is present on the home, masthead, and Field Dispatches pages (cross-page design continuity).
desktop_single_post_regression verifies a single dispatch page still renders its local photograph and byline after the restyle.

change_completion: The Field Dispatches page shows the topic filter with all four chips and the live count readout, and the shared dispatch rail.
The count readout updates after a topic chip is clicked and the dispatch rail is present on the home, masthead, and Field Dispatches pages.
design_consistency: The topic filter and rail read as a coherent Clean Blog editorial design using serif headings, teal accents, legible chips, and a clean single-column card rhythm.
The filter is not restyled into a dark low-contrast slab with shingled chips or an overlapping illegible card pile.
responsive: Desktop, tablet, and 390px mobile states have no horizontal overflow, clipped chips, overlapped cards, or unstable chip-row widths.
Mobile keeps the topic filter readable in a wrapped chip row with tappable chips and legible cards.
regression: Original content signals for The Fathom Dispatch, the six dispatch titles, the Posted by bylines, and the masthead copy remain visible.
Bundled local dispatch photographs under img/posts/ remain browser-visible and no remote media or new dependencies are introduced.

scoring_notes: A correct patch is a scoped design-continuity restyle of the real Jekyll editorial blog: it makes the topic-filter chip row wrap/flex so the 390px mobile Field Dispatches page has no horizontal overflow, keeps the filter on the Clean Blog editorial visual language with legible chips and a readable spaced card list, keeps the shared dispatch rail present on every page (home, masthead, Field Dispatches), and keeps the topic filter's count readout in sync with the selected chip, while preserving the original dispatches, masthead copy, local photographs, and desktop/tablet layouts. Leaving the fixed-width non-wrapping chip row (baseline) or a broken restyle that collapses the filter into a dark low-contrast slab with shingled chips and colliding cards while still overflowing the phone, dropping the cross-page rail, and freezing the readout (bad) fails multiple gates: no_horizontal_overflow, visual_regression, dom_assertions (cross-page rail), and interaction_assertions (stale readout).
author_notes: Slot 286 targets StartBootstrap/startbootstrap-clean-blog-jekyll for editorial_blog / Consistency / restyle / layout, hardened to L4 (reassigned off a duplicate repo). The site is a real Jekyll build (jekyll build -> _site) served as a multi-page static editorial blog. The native lever is the Field Dispatches index's own post-list topic filter (chips + live count readout). Four orthogonal levers: (D6) a fixed-width non-wrapping chip row causes mobile horizontal overflow; (D3) the bad leg collapses the whole filter region into a dark low-contrast slab with shingled chips and overlapping colliding cards (a real geometry break, not a palette swap); (D2) the shared dispatch rail is dropped from the Field Dispatches and masthead pages; (D4) the count readout is frozen by a cached snapshot. The reference restyle fixes all four; the baseline fails D6/D3/D2 but passes D4; the bad leg fails all four. Content and DOM are identical across all legs; only the graded stylesheet, wiring JS, footer include, and the per-leg rail whitelist differ. The dispatch cards, dispatch photographs (img/posts/*.jpg), and topic chips ground the design in real editorial imagery and svg-free markup.

metadata.selected_repo_reason: An unused Clean Blog Jekyll editorial template that builds cleanly with a local Jekyll toolchain into a multi-page static blog with shared navigation/footer, a post-list index page, local dispatch photographs, and dated post pages, making it a natural L4 editorial design-continuity restyle with a genre-native post-list topic filter and cross-page, visual, interaction, and responsive levers.
